chat.author: Ingemar Johansson
chat.text:
I think that regarding delay, unless there is L4S support, there are two ways forward:
1) Avoid delay as much as possible --> low latency in favorable conditions but it becomes overly sensitive to network quirks, like scheduling delay, handover delay ...
2) Accept to build a queue -->  larger latency but more robust to network quirks.
This has been the headache with SCReAM at least

chat.author: Rui Paulo
chat.text:
@Ranysha Ware it's possible that you've answered this already but I was wondering what were your thoughts on the slide where you showed convergence of the different CCAs: how would you define convergence without looking at a graph? How long are we supposed to wait for them to converge? 
are we going to assume that once they converge, they will stay in that state?

chat.author: Ranysha Ware
chat.text:
@Ranysha Ware it's possible that you've answered this already but I was wondering what were your thoughts on the slide where you showed convergence of the different CCAs: how would you define convergence without looking at a graph? How long are we supposed to wait for them to converge?
are we going to assume that once they converge, they will stay in that state?

I don't think anyone asked this. There is an algorithm in the paper that you should check out and there are some slides about it in the backup slides of my presentation. The actual algorithm doesn't define convergence based on looking at it, but we did that when we manually labelled the samples to compare to PACE's output.
We don't answer the question about how long to wait for convergence in the paper but that's a good question. 
What our algorithm attempts to guarantee is that  for the part of the experiment that we said converged, the metric of interest is stable. We don't claim that if you had run the experiment for longer that it would stay converged, but I can see how it is somewhat an implicit assumption.

chat.author: Martin Duke
chat.text: For a NIC that is running pretty hot, I wonder if just round-robining the flows gets you the spacing you need on bottleneck paths, without any timers

chat.author: Michael Welzl
chat.text: You still have the timer at the OS level - this is no worse than today's software pacing. It just spreads out the per-flow minibursts.
